basis: Inherited esophageal achalasia; accompanying autoimmune and sicca findings lack evidence of common direct involvement.
Autoimmune subepidermal blistering; oral involvement varies and is not reliably established above 30%; intestinal inflammation is occasional.
Primary cervical adenocarcinoma; reproductive organs have no axis.
Vertebral and metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia; myopia and auditory canal stenosis occur in only 5-29%.
Lipomatous dysraphic malformation of the spinal conus; possible neurogenic bowel, bladder and limb dysfunction does not establish direct additional organ damage.
Microcephaly defines the syndrome; dilated cardiomyopathy occurs in 4/9. Recurrent infections alone do not establish intrinsic immunodeficiency.
Isolated inherited progressive hearing loss.
Ritscher-Schinzel syndrome is defined by cerebellar malformations, developmental impairment and congenital cardiac defects; other anomalies are variable.
Neoplasm of the paraurethral glands, classified as vulvar reproductive tissue; urethral involvement is not established.
Malignant soft-tissue tumor with skeletal muscle differentiation, usually arising in the extremities.
Invasive pneumococcal bloodstream infection; bacteremia alone does not establish blood-cell or coagulation disease.
Fibrosing panniculitis damages skin and subcutaneous tissue; associated venous insufficiency is a separate condition.
Intellectual disability, retinal dystrophy and neutropenia define Cohen syndrome; dental/tongue/gingival abnormalities occur in 80-99%; joint abnormalities omitted under cap.
Ectodermal dysplasia restricted to hair and nails.
Umbrella of skeletal titin myopathies; cardiac disease varies by subtype. Respiratory insufficiency commonly reflects muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Anterior segment malformation with corneal abnormalities and developmental glaucoma.
THRA thyroid-hormone resistance; skeletal maturation defects, developmental impairment and anemia each affect >30%; constipation alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Acquired impairment of immune function; specific infections and their organ complications are separate diseases.
Inherited palmoplantar epidermal hyperkeratosis with hyperhidrosis.
Immune-complex glomerular injury; hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia are occasional. Associated hypertension is separately diagnosed.
Skeletal anomalies and impaired intellectual development define this syndrome group.
Familial immune-mediated cutaneous lichen planus; oral disease frequency is not established above 30% for this subtype.
Benign tumor arising in the ocular choroid; vascular ancestry does not establish systemic cardiovascular involvement.
Protein and energy deficiency causes metabolic depletion; skeletal muscle wasting affects most patients (>50%). Skin and hepatic changes vary by subtype.
Creatine biosynthesis defects cause cerebral creatine deficiency; developmental and cognitive impairment affect most patients (>80%).
